subject: project-nereid
label: The clinic gets its front door
from: A place named across a dozen records and never once described
to: THE PARLOUR, THE CONSENT LADDER AND THE GUMMY — three system records
note:
EVERY WOMAN MEETS THE IMAGINED CLINIC FIRST: fluorescent panels, a clipboard before a hello, the wrong name called off a record and the injury treated as DATABASE WEATHER. She rehearses her corrections on the way over. Then the door opens with a brass chime onto honey floorboards, mismatched vases and one astonishing mustard chair.

IT IS CLINIC-SHAPED AND NOT CLINIC-DESIGNED. Cassandra decorated it the way she decorates everything, and the philosophy underneath is not soft at all: she remembered the rooms she was once expected to defend herself in, and could not rewrite anyone's journey to the clinic — only WHAT MET THEM AT ITS END.

THE DELIVERY MECHANISM IS NOW ON THE RECORD AND THE ARCHIVE NEVER HAD IT. Nereid arrives as ONE CONSENT-LOCKED GUMMY, cooked from her own Final Authorization, in a mould family she chose: shark, dinosaur, animal, car. There are no gummy candies in the parlour, deliberately, so nothing in a communal bowl can blur what that object is.

AND THE LADDER: entering was not consent, sitting was not consent, tea was not consent, reading page one is not consent. IMMUTABLE CORE, then CONSENT MENU, then a REVIEW OF THE WHOLE BODY, then FINAL AUTHORIZATION — and review never becomes authorization merely because the clinic likes the design.
